d: An overview of legacy Sound objects and effects.
h:
There is a newer set of audio objects and effects that offer more control and address robust use cases. For more information, see Audio.

Sound effects and music enhance your games and make them more immersive. You can import your own audio assets or search for free-to-use audio in the Creator Store, play audio through Sound or objects, and enhance audio playback through dynamic effects.

Sound objects

A sound object emits audio within a game. Roblox assigns each audio asset a unique ID that you can assign to Sound objects to play a specific sound effect or music track. You can either set this audio to play automatically at runtime, or trigger it to play from scripts.

The location of where you place a Sound object in the Explorer hierarchy affects how users hear audio. If you want users to only hear audio near a specific position, you must parent the Sound object to a 3D object or Attachment to behave as positional audio. If you want users to hear audio regardless of their position, you must insert the Sound object directly into Workspace or SoundService to behave as background audio.

Sound groups

A sound group acts as an audio mixer for multiple audio objects, such as Sound objects or additional SoundGroups, allowing you to control the volume and dynamic effects properties of multiple audio signals at once.

Dynamic effects

Dynamic effects modify or enhance the audio of individual Sound objects or an entire SoundGroup. You can apply these effects to make audio more immersive within the game, such as using EqualizerSoundEffect to make rain sound muffled, CompressorSoundEffect to control a sound's maximum volume, or ReverbSoundEffect to add more realistic reflections of sound in interior spaces.

kid.simple: This page introduces the older way to add sound in Roblox, using the `Sound` object. Roblox now has a newer set of audio objects that can do more, but `Sound` still shows up in lots of games and tutorials, so it helps to know it. Where you put a `Sound` in the Explorer decides whether players hear it everywhere or only near a spot. You can also group sounds together and add effects like echo or muffling.
kid.analogy: A `Sound` inside a part is like a radio sitting on a table: you hear it louder as you walk up to it. A `Sound` in SoundService is like music in your headphones: the same wherever you go.
keyPoints: This is the legacy (older) sound system; the newer audio objects are recommended for new work.
Each audio file has an ID you put into a `Sound` object's `SoundId` to choose what it plays.
A sound can play automatically when the game starts, or a script can start it.
Put a `Sound` inside a part or `Attachment` to make it positional, so players only hear it nearby.
Put a `Sound` directly in Workspace or SoundService to make it background audio heard everywhere.
A `SoundGroup` works like a mixer that controls the volume and effects of many sounds at once.
Dynamic effects like `EqualizerSoundEffect`, `CompressorSoundEffect`, and `ReverbSoundEffect` change how a sound or group sounds.

terms.legacy: An older feature that still works but has a newer replacement.
terms.audio asset: A sound file uploaded to Roblox, with its own ID number.
terms.runtime: When the game is actually running and being played.
terms.positional audio: Sound that comes from a spot in the world and gets quieter as you move away from it.
terms.background audio: Sound that is the same volume no matter where you stand, like a soundtrack.
terms.parent: The object something sits inside in the Explorer. If a `Sound` is inside a part, the part is its parent.
terms.audio mixer: A tool that lets you adjust the volume of many sounds together, like sliders on a DJ board.
terms.dynamic effect: An object that changes how a sound comes out, like adding echo or muffling it.

watchOut: If you want everyone to hear music everywhere, do not put the `Sound` inside a part. Put it in SoundService or Workspace.
If a sound seems to play from nowhere, check its parent; a `Sound` in Workspace plays for the whole game.
For brand-new projects, try the newer audio objects first, since `Sound` is the older system.
